vulnerability.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
vulnerability.description: Attacks that force users to execute unwanted actions
patterns: CSRF via SVG or image upload
vulnerability.impact: Unauthorized actions performed on behalf of authenticated users
vulnerability.mitigation: Use CSRF tokens, SameSite cookies, and verify request origins

findings.title: Missing CSRF Token
findings.vulnerable_code:
function sendTo(address receiver, uint amount) public require(tx.origin == owner);
receiver.transfer(amount);
findings.explanation: The function does not include a CSRF token, making it vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actions can be performed on behalf of authenticated users.
exploitation_steps: Send a malicious tx.origin request to the contract, tricking it into executing the transfer function.
findings.remediation: Include a CSRF token in the transfer function and validate its presence.

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery
findings.explanation: The call() function executes a function with no return value, making it vulnerable to Reentrancy attacks.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actions can be performed on behalf of authenticated users
exploitation_steps: Send a malicious request to the withdrawFunds function with a forged sender address.
Exploit the call() function's lack of return value.

findings.title: Vulnerable Code
findings.explanation: The `CashOut` function calls `msg.sender.call.value(_am)` which allows an attacker to trick the user into executing arbitrary code on their behalf.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actions performed on behalf of authenticated users
exploitation_steps: 1. Send a malicious request to /cashout with a large amount (_am).
example_payloads:
POST /cashout HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Content-Length: 0

100 ether
findings.remediation: Verify request origins and validate user input.

findings.title: Missing CSRF Token
findings.explanation: The function calls msg.sender's `call()` method without verifying a CSRF token, making it vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actions can be performed on behalf of authenticated users.
exploitation_steps: Attacker sends a POST request to /withdraw with a malicious amount
The attacker's request is accepted, and the malicious amount is executed
findings.exploitation_conditions: Authenticated users can reach the /withdraw endpoint.
findings.remediation: Add a CSRF token verification in the `withdraw` function.

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.vulnerable_code: function solve(string solution) public { require(hash == sha3(solution)); msg.sender.transfer(1000 ether); }
findings.explanation: This contract lacks a CSRF token, allowing an attacker to transfer Ether from the contract on behalf of the user.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actions performed on behalf of authenticated users can lead to financial losses or compromise the account.
exploitation_steps: Attacker sends a POST request to /solve with a crafted solution string.
findings.exploitation_conditions: User is authenticated and authorized to execute the solve function.
findings.remediation: Implement a CSRF token mechanism, such as reCAPTCHA or a library like CSRF-Fortify.

findings.title: Missing CSRF Token
findings.explanation: The setReward() function does not include a CSRF token, making it vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks.
findings.impact: An attacker could force the owner to transfer funds without their knowledge or consent.
exploitation_steps: An attacker sends a malicious request to the setReward() function with a fake owner address.
findings.exploitation_conditions: The owner is authenticated and has not claimed the reward yet.
findings.remediation: Add a CSRF token to the setReward() function

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery
findings.explanation: The `play` function accepts a user-provided `number` parameter without proper validation, allowing an attacker to manipulate the game state.
findings.impact: An attacker could force the game to send Ether to another player's address.
exploitation_steps: Send a request with a forged `number` parameter to manipulate the game state.
findings.exploitation_conditions: The attacker needs access to the contract's memory or can execute arbitrary transactions.
findings.remediation: Validate user input and ensure proper authorization checks are in place.

findings.title: Vulnerable Code
findings.explanation: The function does not verify the request origin before executing a transaction.
findings.impact: Unauthorized transactions can be executed without user consent.
exploitation_steps: An attacker requests a transaction for an invalid address
The system executes the transaction without verifying the request origin
findings.exploitation_conditions: The attacker can request a transaction with an invalid address.
findings.remediation: Verify the request origin before executing a transaction.

findings.title: Vulnerable event call without CSRF token
findings.vulnerable_code: event SingleTransact(address owner, uint value, address to, bytes data, address created);
findings.explanation: The `SingleTransact` event call does not include a CSRF token, making it vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks.
findings.impact: An attacker could trick an authorized user into executing unintended transactions on their behalf.
exploitation_steps: An attacker sends a malicious SingleTransact event call to the contract.
The contract executes the transaction without verification, allowing the attacker to control the outcome.
findings.exploitation_conditions: Attacker has access to authorized user's credentials or can trick them into executing the malicious event call.
findings.remediation: Always include a CSRF token in sensitive event calls, such as `SingleTransact`.
findings.secure_code_example: event SingleTransact(address owner, uint value, address to, bytes data, address created) { require(msg.sender == owner || owner(msg.sender)); }

chunk_analyses.notes: The contract's use of vulnerable event calls and lack of input validation make it susceptible to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks.

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
findings.explanation: The execute function does not verify the validity of the request data. An attacker can submit a malicious request by manipulating the 'msg.data' variable.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actions performed on behalf of authenticated users.
exploitation_steps: Manipulate the request data to execute unintended actions
Use the attacker-controlled data to bypass authentication checks
findings.exploitation_conditions: The attacker needs to reach the POST /transfer endpoint while authenticated.
findings.remediation: Verify the validity of the request data by using CSRF tokens or similar protection mechanisms

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery
findings.explanation: The function does not verify the origin of the request before executing it, making it vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actions can be performed on behalf of authenticated users.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
External Request -> underLimit/required check -> Execution
 External Request -> Reveal Origin Check (Missing) -> Execution
exploitation_steps: User sends malicious payload to the target address.
Malicious payload is executed without origin verification.
findings.exploitation_conditions: Target contract has _required = 1 or _to is a valid address.
findings.remediation: Verify the origin of the request before executing it.

findings.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery
findings.vulnerable_code: function hasConfirmed(bytes32 _operation, address _owner) external constant returns (bool) { return _walletLibrary.delegatecall(msg.data); }
findings.explanation: The function does not verify the origin of the request before making a delegated call to another contract.
findings.impact: Unauthorized actions can be performed on behalf of authenticated users if the delegated contract is compromised.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
External Request -> delegatecall -> External Contract
 External Request -> Reveal Origin Check (Missing) -> Delegation
exploitation_steps: User sends malicious payload to the target contract.
Malicious payload is delegated without origin verification.
findings.exploitation_conditions: Target contract has _walletLibrary.delegatecall with invalid msg.data.
findings.remediation: Verify the origin of the request before making a delegated call to another contract.
findings.secure_code_example: function hasConfirmed(bytes32 _operation, address _owner) external constant returns (bool) { require(_msg.sender == owner); return true; }

findings.title: Potential CSRF vulnerability
findings.explanation: The `setDailyLimit` function uses `onlymanyowners` modifier, which seems to protect against reentrancy attacks, but may not prevent CSRF attacks since the same modifier is used in other functions (e.g., `initWallet`, `kill`).
findings.impact: Unauthorized changes to daily spending limits.
exploitation_steps: Send a request with malicious data to the /setDailyLimit endpoint.
findings.remediation: Use `onlyowner` modifier instead of `onlymanyowners` for sensitive functions.

function execute(address _to, uint _value, bytes _data) external onlyowner returns (bytes32 o_hash) {
  // ...
findings.explanation: The `execute` function does not verify the origin of the request before executing a transaction.

findings.title: Missing SameSite Cookie
findings.explanation: The contract does not set a SameSite attribute for its cookies, making them vulnerable to CSRF attacks.
findings.impact: An attacker could potentially trick users into executing unintended transactions on their behalf.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
GET /execute HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Cookie: session_id=1234567890
Accept: */*
Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.5
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br
Connection: keep-alive
Referer: https://example.com/referer
exploitation_steps: The attacker crafts a malicious URL that includes a CSRF token, which is then included in the request.
The contract verifies the CSRF token and executes the transaction on behalf of the user.
findings.exploitation_conditions: The attacker can reach POST /execute while authenticated.
findings.remediation: Set the SameSite attribute for all cookies to prevent CSRF attacks.

chunk_analyses.notes: This contract is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery due to missing SameSite cookie attributes.
